title: MovieSwiftUI
description: Build a SwiftUI movie-discovery mini app with catalogue mapping, search, genre selection, sorting, detail pages, and a persistent watchlist.
problem: Learners need a source-grounded way to understand and extend MovieSwiftUI while separating implemented behavior from demo data, simulations, and missing integrations.
audience: Third-year undergraduate students who have completed introductory programming and want a practical mobile mini-project.
prerequisites: Git basics and ability to run the platform tooling described in the source README
learning_outcomes: Explain and trace movie fields, identity, movieinfo projection, and seed records in its named source files.
Explain and trace response decoding/mapping and missing-field rejection in its named source files.
Explain and trace text search fields, genre filtering, rating/year ordering, and ui controls in its named source files.
Explain and trace store defaults, add/remove operations, and userdefaults reload in its named source files.
Explain and trace navigation, card poster rendering, shared store, and detail fields in its named source files.
Explain and trace mapping/filter tests, watchlist persistence tests, xcodegen targets, and simulator review in its named source files.
Distinguish unit-test evidence from device, service, and deployment evidence.
Propose a safe, bounded extension without describing it as already implemented.
